title: Version cap must be enforced against the persisted GVK, not the declared one
answers: Why does apistore reject a write even though the request declared an allowed version?
How is the max-allowed-version policy checked during storage writes?
Can a codec/serializer that upconverts bypass the version cap?
body: `Storage.encode` (pkg/storage/unified/apistore/prepare.go: `Storage.encode`) always serializes first, then checks `VersionPolicy.HasMaxAllowed` against the version actually persisted (read back via `persistedVersion`, not the object's requested/declared version). This matters because a codec or custom Serializer can upconvert to a higher-priority storage version than the caller requested; checking the declared version would let an over-cap write slip through. A persisted GVK from outside the resource's group is rejected outright (cannot be ranked against the group's cap). `enforceCap=true` on create and non-deletion updates; `enforceCap=false` for deletion-related writes (soft delete, finalizer/status writes while `deletionTimestamp` is set) so an already over-cap object stays removable.
applies: Any write path through pkg/storage/unified/apistore.Storage for a resource group with a VersionPolicy max-allowed-version cap.
